sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Highland County
sections.html:
Three Hillsboro offices split the work. The auditor sets values and keeps the tax list, the treasurer sends bills and takes payment, and the recorder files the deeds that change the name on a parcel. The auditor is also the county's chief fiscal officer and appraiser-in-chief for real estate, and it hands collected tax out to villages, townships and school districts.

sections.h2: How a Highland County house is valued for tax
sections.html:
Values are revisited every three years, and Ohio taxes 35% of appraised market value. Millage for the school district, township or village and any levies at the parcel's location then turns that taxable value into a bill.

Two neighbors on one road can be billed at different rates if a district line runs between them, so pull the parcel's own record instead of copying a nearby bill.

The auditor counts 32,381 parcels as of 2024, against 19,196 housing units, so parcels outnumber homes by a wide margin. The gap points to farmland, woodland and vacant lots, and it makes the farm valuation rules further down worth reading even for a town seller.

sections.h2: Payment dates and how to pay
sections.html:
Taxes are paid in two halves each year, and the treasurer's page posts the due date for each half. A seller who closes after either date should ask the treasurer to confirm the half was posted.

Payment options on that page include an online link and a toll-free line, 1-844-920-3600. By mail, the address is P.O. Box 824, Hillsboro, OH 45133. The treasurer's own phone is 937-393-9951.

Back taxes belong to the same office. The auditor's tools menu includes a delinquency report, and the treasurer can say what a past-due balance would add to a payoff. A title company will request that payoff whatever the answer.

An owner who thinks the value is wrong files a complaint with the auditor, and the county Board of Revision hears it. Section 5715.19 sets the deadline at March 31 of the next tax year, or the day first-half collection closes if that is later. The complaint has to state how much overvaluation or undervaluation it claims.

Three forms on the auditor's site cover most cases:

  • DTE 1 for a complaint about the value of real property.
  • DTE 1M for a manufactured or mobile home taxed like real property.
  • DTE 2 for a complaint about an assessment other than market value.

While a complaint is pending the owner may pay on the value claimed, and the statute makes the complainant hand over all evidence in the owner's knowledge. A recent arm's-length sale is the strongest proof, and the auditor's sales report shows what neighbors' parcels brought.

sections.h2: Forms that reduce a tax bill
sections.html:
The auditor sorts relief forms by type:

  • Homestead: DTE 105A for seniors, disabled persons and surviving spouses, DTE 105I for disabled military service members and their surviving spouses, and DTE 105K for surviving spouses of public service officers killed in the line of duty.
  • Owner occupancy: DTE 105C for real property and DTE 56 for taxed manufactured homes.
  • Damage: DTE 26 for destroyed or damaged real property and DTE 49 for a manufactured home.
  • Exemptions: DTE 23 for tax-exempt owners and DTE 23V for service and fraternal organizations.

Filing windows and income limits move with the tax year, so ask the Highland County Auditor which apply to you before relying on a form from memory.

The current agricultural use valuation program taxes qualifying farmland on its farm income instead of its market price. Land of 10 or more acres, not counting the homesite, qualifies if used exclusively for agriculture. Smaller tracts qualify with gross income of at least $2,500 in each of the past three years. The first application costs $25 and must be filed before the first Monday in March, and renewals are mailed to owners each year.

Leaving the program is expensive. Land removed from it owes a recoupment charge equal to three years of the tax savings, whether the owner missed a renewal or changed the use. Woodland cannot take both the farm program and the older forestry savings, and the farm program needs a management plan from a forester that the auditor approves.

A sale brings the program into the paperwork. Section 319.202 has the buyer's statement report whether the parcel was enrolled, and the auditor's forms include DTE 102 for such a conveyance. A farm seller should ask for the likely recoupment figure before accepting an offer.

sections.h2: Tax records to gather before listing
sections.html:
A short folder saves days with a buyer's title company. Pull these items from the county's own sites:

  • The parcel record from the auditor's search page, which shows the owner of record, the valuation and the tax history.
  • The treasurer's payment status for both halves of the current year, plus any past-due balance from the delinquency report.
  • Proof of any homestead or owner occupancy reduction you now receive, because the buyer's value statement must say whether the seller's taxes are reduced.
  • Any farm valuation enrollment, with the three-year recoupment exposure in mind.

The auditor's conveyance fee calculator, which includes a parcel transfer fee, gives a rough closing cost before the county's final figure. The auditor's page lists the Ohio conveyance statement forms, DTE 100 and DTE 100EX, next to the homestead and farm conveyance statements, so the right paper is easy to find.

Hillsboro is the county seat of this hilly county of about 553 square miles. The 2025 estimate is 43,823 people. Owners live in 74.3% of occupied homes, the median home value is $168,900, and median household income is $65,785.

A seller behind on payments can begin at the treasurer, then ask the auditor for the parcel's tax history before negotiating. The recorder and auditor share the 119 Governor Foraker Place address, so a deed question and a valuation question can often be handled in one trip.

Unpaid tax on a parcel shows up in the title search, and it is paid out of the seller's proceeds at closing. Ask the treasurer for the current balance and the auditor for the tax history, then give both to your closing agent. If the balance is large, find out early whether a payment arrangement is possible so the sale can move on schedule.

faqs.q: Who bills property tax in Highland County?
faqs.a: The Highland County Treasurer. The mailing address is P.O. Box 824 in Hillsboro, the phone is 937-393-9951, and the treasurer's page also takes payments online.

faqs.q: What share of market value does Ohio tax?
faqs.a: 35%. Values are revisited every three years.

faqs.q: What is the deadline for a valuation complaint?
faqs.a: March 31 of the next tax year, or the close of first-half collection if that falls later. File form DTE 1 with the auditor and expect a Board of Revision hearing.

faqs.q: Does the county have a farmland program?
faqs.a: Yes, current agricultural use valuation. It requires exclusive agricultural use and a $25 first application filed before the first Monday in March.

faqs.q: What happens if farmland stops qualifying?
faqs.a: The owner pays a recoupment charge equal to the tax savings of the last three years. Ask the auditor for an estimate before you sign a sale contract.
